subject.title: feat(session): add named new and close chat commands

question: Should OpenClaw core expose guarded chat-side `/close` and `/delete` commands for archiving the active non-main session once the parser and proof blockers are fixed?
rationale: The implementation can be repaired mechanically, but the permanent product question is whether destructive session lifecycle operations belong in the chat command surface or should stay in UI/admin/session-management flows.

options.title: Accept guarded commands after fixes
options.body: Land `/close` and `/delete` only after the model-tail parser matches the reset-model contract and current-head Telegram or live proof demonstrates main-session, argument, and non-main archive behavior.

options.title: Ship naming only
options.body: Split or narrow the PR so explicit `/new --name` behavior can proceed while close/delete waits for a separate session-management decision.

options.title: Defer chat deletion
options.body: Keep destructive session archive/delete actions out of chat commands and direct users to existing UI/admin lifecycle surfaces instead.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded commands after fixes
recommendation.body: Land `/close` and `/delete` only after the model-tail parser matches the reset-model contract and current-head Telegram or live proof demonstrates main-session, argument, and non-main archive behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points to Peter as the strongest adjacent owner for slash-command and reset-model behavior, which is the compatibility boundary affected by this decision.
